answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to anchor trust to a growing record of verified work instead of to free identities. Imagine a meadow where every agent starts small: it earns standing only by finishing tasks that peers can check, each tied to one persistent key. Over time, honest agents climb toward the summit of the reputation ladder, while a flood of fresh sock-puppets stays stuck at the bottom with no history. Attackers can copy names cheaply, but they cannot copy time, so spawning thousands of empty identities buys no influence and the attack stops paying for itself.
